subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the circle passing through the point (−2,14) and concentric with x² + y² − 6x − 4y − 12 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.78 — VSAQ chapter 12 Circle, answer 109.1. Printed appearance tag: TS 17. insider_note: Concentric means the same centre, so only the constant term may change — copy the x and y terms exactly and put an unknown k in place of the constant.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the concentric family
steps.margin_note: One mark. Copy −6x and −4y exactly; changing either of them moves the centre.
steps.memory_tip: Concentric circles share g and f. Only c changes.
lines: Concentric circles have the same centre,
so g and f are unchanged and only c differs.
steps.why: The centre is (−g, −f), so two circles are concentric exactly when they share g and f. Only the constant is free, and it fixes the radius.
common_mistakes: Changing the sign of the x or y term while copying.
Trying to find the centre first, which is not needed.

steps.label: Substitute the point and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 14² = 196, which is the number most often slipped here.
steps.memory_tip: Put the point in and solve one linear equation in k.
steps.why: A point lies on a circle exactly when it satisfies the equation, so substituting it turns the unknown constant into a one-step calculation.
